_format: Golden cases for Slovo's text pipeline (SPEC 4.3 step 2 and 4.5). The macOS app checks them in Tests/SlovoCoreTests/SharedTextPipelineFixtureTests.swift; the Windows port must produce the same `expected` for every case.

The pipeline turns `input` (a raw engine transcript) into the inserted text in five stages, in this order: snippets, dictionary replacements, dictionary terms (fuzzy correction), auto cleanup (fillers, repetitions, spacing), style.
cases[].name: a unique id. cases[].input: the transcript.

context.dictionary: the Dictionary in its stored order, [{"kind": "term" | "replacement", "text", "replacement"}]. `text` is the term, or the `from` phrase of a replacement; `replacement` is the `to` text (absent for terms).
context.cleanup: {"removeFillers": bool, "removeRepetitions": bool}; both false turns auto cleanup off entirely, spacing fixes included.
context.style: "formal" | "casual" | "veryCasual" | null; null leaves casing and punctuation as the earlier stages left them.
context.languageMode: "mixed" | "russian" | "english"; carried for completeness, no stage reads it yet.

lexicon: the spelling dictionaries used INSTEAD of the system spell checker, {languageCode: [words]} with codes "ru" and "en". A language absent from the object has no dictionary at all (different from an empty list, which is a dictionary that knows no words). isCorrect(word, language) is true when the list holds `word` exactly or holds its lowercase form: a lowercase entry accepts any casing, a capitalized entry such as "Москва" accepts only that casing. Words with Cyrillic letters are checked against "ru", words with Latin letters against "en".
expected: {"text", "snippetsApplied", "replacementsApplied", "termFixesApplied"}, the pipeline's result and its counters.

Text semantics to match: positions are extended grapheme clusters (Swift Character); a letter is a cluster whose first scalar is Unicode Alphabetic, a number one whose first scalar has a numeric type; case mapping is full Unicode mapping (ß uppercases to SS, and a mapping that changes the cluster count is skipped); comparisons fold ё to е and ’ to '; strings compare by canonical equivalence, so normalize input to NFC.

Constants that live in code rather than here: filler lists, abbreviation lists, the borrowed-name list, edit-distance thresholds (0.34, 4 letters) and the spelling-key rules; see Sources/SlovoCore/Text.
To regenerate `expected` after an intended change: SLOVO_REGENERATE_FIXTURES=1 swift test --filter SharedTextPipelineFixtureTests, then review the diff.
